description: Every design §6.4 recovery row, as a scenario with scripted process reality. `recover` folds the journal to expected state, probes reality (shim fingerprint + process-group scan for liveness, then the outcome file, nonce-checked), and classifies per TEP §12.2. Never blind-respawns.

rows.name: spawn-intended-absent
rows.notes: the intent was journaled but never completed spawning

rows.name: orphaned-under-dead-shim

reality.note: env-tagged live process/group with no live shim

rows.notes: custody is unrecoverable — no shim can capture the outcome; a reconciliation event names the killed PIDs

rows.name: matching
rows.notes: re-arm relative timers from exec-started on the monotonic clock (§6.6)

rows.name: matching-late
rows.notes: process gone, outcome file present and nonce-verified

rows.name: stale-foreign-nonce-mismatch
rows.notes: treated as absent — reconciled as if no outcome existed

rows.name: harvesting-resume
rows.notes: out/ is frozen once the process is gone — re-collection is deterministic and never drops outputs a partial harvest missed; then record and terminalize

rows.name: recording-resume
rows.notes: never re-assemble the Delivery — re-write verbatim from the seal-once checkpoint (§9.1), then emit delivery-recorded and terminalize

rows.name: terminal-with-survivors
rows.notes: the terminal record wins; survivors get the kill ladder; a reconciliation event is appended

rows.name: lost-then-corrective
rows.notes: TEP §10.4 rule 6 — the ONE sanctioned terminal-to-terminal transition; every other terminal-to-terminal transition is contradictory
